messages:
Maria Chen: FYI we just got an escalated support ticket from a customer (Acme) — they say JSON payloads coming back from our chat->structured-output endpoint started dropping required fields after yesterday's rollout. They attached example requests and outputs. They say it started at ~09:12 PST. Ticket ID #CS-9843.

Maria Chen: customer pasted expected schema + actual output. Expected 'order_id' and 'items[].price' to be present, but many responses have order_id null or items array missing price keys entirely. They included request_id headers: req_8f3a7c, req_8f3a8, req_8f3b01.

Jamal Patel: ack. Are these requests routed to hosted or dedicated?

Maria Chen: Hosted (standard tier). Region us-west. They said model param = "redwood-open-structured-v2" in the payload.

Olivia Gomez: Any sign of auth/billing issues? 401/402 would show different symptom.

Maria Chen: No auth errors — all 200s. Billing-bot didn't flag anything. They did mention one earlier 429 spike around 09:05 but these responses are 200 with malformed content.

Jamal Patel: Can we get the raw responses? Maria, paste one of the API responses and the prompt they used.

Maria Chen: pasted: ```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-open-structured-v2",
  "input": "Extract order as JSON according to schema",
  "response_format": {"type":"json_schema","schema":{
    "type":"object",
    "required":["order_id","items"],
    "properties":{
      "order_id":{"type":"string"},
      "items":{"type":"array","items":{
        "type":"object","required":["sku","price"],"properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"price":{"type":"number"}}
      }}
    }
  }}
}
```

Maria Chen: Actual response body for req_8f3a7c: ```
{
  "order_id": null,
  "items": [
    {"sku":"ABC123"},
    {"sku":"XYZ987","price":49.99}
  ]
}
```

Jamal Patel: interesting — one item has price, one missing. That smells like post-processing / strict schema enforcement failing intermittently. Does any log show a schema-assertion error or fallback?

Maria Chen: customer included our response headers: X-Model-Version: v2.1.3, X-Inference-Pipeline: standard, X-Postproc: json-strict. They also forwarded our trace id: trace-20260312-5521.

Tai Huang: I'm oncall — pulling traces for trace-20260312-5521. Give me 2 min.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout v3.8.2 -> 3.9.0 started 2026-03-11T23:40Z, canary completed 2026-03-12T02:10Z.

Tai Huang: trace shows requests for that time hit backend host host-gpu-17. I see a config toggle changed in deployment 3.9.0: postproc.strict_mode=false for some routes — suspicious.

Jamal Patel: Wait postproc.strict_mode=false would normally be more permissive, not drop fields. Could toggling strict_mode cause partial suppression when outputs don't exactly match schema? Need to check postproc code path.

Olivia Gomez: Customer reports they didn't change prompts. They provided a repro harness (curl) — Maria can you upload?

Maria Chen: uploaded repro snippet: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-structured-v2","input":"Order: SKU ABC123 qty 1 price $-","response_format":{"type":"json_schema","schema":{...}}}'
```

Jamal Patel: I'll run the repro locally against prod endpoint (non-prod env doesn't have v3.9.0 changes). If I can reproduce we can bisect between model and postproc.

Jamal Patel: ran against prod, got same null order_id and missing price on first item. Request id req_9b4c11.

Jamal Patel: Running with model pinned to redwood-open-structured-v2@v2.1.2 (previous) via model_version header — output matches expected: order_id present, both items have price. So newer model(or runtime combo) seems to correlate.

Tai Huang: I pulled service config diffs from the rollout — we toggled a small change: enable_kv_cache=true for short prompts + disabled a schema-normalizer micro-optimization (intended to reduce latency). The normalizer fills inferred numeric fields when present as '$49.99' strings and coerces types. If normalizer was disabled, we'd expect prices to be strings, not missing. But we see missing keys entirely.

Jamal Patel: That suggests postproc might prune fields when coercion fails. If the normalizer returned null, downstream postproc might drop that key to avoid schema violations.

Olivia Gomez: Customer also included latency numbers: median latency ~210ms, p95 ~720ms this morning, same cluster. They noticed a small improvement p50 after rollout, so toggles did something.

Maria Chen: Customer is pushing for a quick rollback — they depend on strict schema for ingestion. They're asking for ETA.

Jamal Patel: Proposed immediate steps: 1) rollback canary change that disabled normalizer for structured routes or re-enable schema-normalizer; 2) add a defensive fix in postproc to never drop required keys (emit null but keep key); 3) run regression tests against customer prompt set.

Tai Huang: I can cherry-pick a hotfix to re-enable normalizer for routes matching response_format=json_schema. Patching now.

deploy-bot: Patch PR #3486 created by @tai and deployed to canary group 3.9.1-canary at 2026-03-12T10:03Z.

Jamal Patel: Running the customer's repro against 3.9.1-canary... good news: order_id present, items[].price present as numbers now. Repro request req_9b6d44.

Maria Chen: I messaged the customer with interim: we've deployed a targeted hotfix to re-enable schema normalizer for structured outputs, can you confirm on your side?

Maria Chen: Customer responded: "we ran our ingestion tests, looks good so far for 500 samples, still running a full sweep, will update." :thumbsup:

Olivia Gomez: Action items: - Jamal to add a unit/regression test covering price coercion + required-key preservation. - Tai to follow up with a full rollback plan if more regressions reported. - Maria to update ticket CS-9843 and schedule a customer call if full sweep fails. - Product to review rollout checklist for postproc toggles.

Jamal Patel: I'll open an internal CR with the failing test vectors from Acme and add it to the pre-rollout test harness.

billing-bot: Note: no billing events triggered for CS-9843.

Maria Chen: Thanks team — I'll keep thread updated. If customer completes full sweep OK, I'll close the ticket and send a short postmortem. If any of you see repeat failures, ping me. :eyes:

Tai Huang: marking oncall note and will pair with jamal tonight to run broad regression across other structured schemas.

Maria Chen: Closing loop — customer reported green on full sweep at 2026-03-12T12:01Z. They asked for a short postmortem and timeline for root cause. I'll file follow-up.

Jamal Patel: Root cause summary (to add to PM): a micro-optimization in rollout 3.9.0 disabled a schema-normalizer for certain short-sequence routes; without normalization, coercion returned nulls for some tokens which caused postproc to prune required keys; hotfix re-enabled normalizer for json_schema routes and added defensive behavior to preserve keys even on coercion failure.

Maria Chen: Thanks all — filing postmortem and customer communication now. :white_check_mark:
